nodes.text: Sato et al. 2014, overview of Y-chromosome variation in modern Japanese males.
Sato et al. 2014 reports Y-chromosome haplogroup variation in modern Japanese male populations.
D1a2a/D-M55 persists at high frequency in modern Japanese male lineages.
High D1a2a/D-M55 frequency coexists with largely continental-derived autosomal ancestry in many mainland Japanese population models.
Y-chromosome asymmetry can preserve signals of sex-biased social structure or reproductive advantage.
Paternal-lineage asymmetry may reflect some form of social or reproductive advantage rather than passive survival alone.
Autosomal ancestry models do not by themselves explain the social-historical meaning of paternal-lineage asymmetry.
Paternal-lineage asymmetry may indicate some form of social or reproductive advantage for Jomon-associated paternal lineages.
D1a2a/D-M55 persistence is best understood as passive Jomon-associated survival.
Hudson 1992 on Yayoi ritual and dotaku context.
Dotaku ritual flourished and then ended in the Late Yayoi period.
The end of dotaku ritual may reflect social reorganization or network disruption, not solely internal cultural transformation.
Dotaku discontinuity is usually treated as internal ritual transformation or cultural transition.
component_claims: Dotaku ritual discontinuity is an internal cultural transition

nodes.text: Kiki myths may preserve structures of ritual-political memory related to social integration.
Kiki mythic material is often treated as literary-theological tradition rather than usable social-historical memory.
component_claims: Mythic structures are difficult to connect to social process

nodes.text: The Kojiki and Nihon Shoki contain mythic complexes involving descent, land transfer, agricultural origins, and ritual-political legitimacy.
Y-chromosome frequency alone cannot prove conquest or elite dominance.
nodes.why_risky: Frequency asymmetry can arise through multiple demographic and sampling processes.
nodes.suggested_patch: State this as a testable possibility and list alternative explanations.
nodes.failure_mode_notes: A lineage-frequency observation cannot by itself carry a conquest or elite-dominance conclusion.

nodes.text: Dotaku discontinuity alone cannot prove external disruption or political takeover.
nodes.why_risky: Internal ritual transformation may explain discontinuity without external social disruption.
nodes.suggested_patch: Frame disruption as one possible interpretation requiring independent support.
nodes.failure_mode_notes: A ritual discontinuity can be captured by a disruption narrative before local continuity and chronology are checked.

nodes.text: Kiki mythic structures cannot be read as literal historical record.
nodes.why_risky: Mythic correspondences can be overread without independent controls.
nodes.suggested_patch: Use method language: possible transformed memory structure, not direct evidence.
nodes.failure_mode_notes: Mythic motifs are interpretive analogies and cannot be laundered into literal historical evidence.

nodes.text: If representative Kofun elite burials do not show elevated D1a2a/D-M55 compared with non-elites, the paternal-elite version is weakened.
nodes.required_evidence: Representative ancient DNA from elite and non-elite Kofun burials.

nodes.text: If dotaku discontinuity is fully explained by local ritual transformation with no social network disruption, UC2 is weakened.
nodes.required_evidence: Regional archaeological sequences showing continuous local transformation without disruption.

nodes.text: If Kiki descent and land-transfer motifs are late literary constructions with no stable earlier pattern, UC3 is weakened.
nodes.required_evidence: Textual-historical evidence for late invention or unstable transmission of the relevant motifs.

nodes.text: Comparative cases are possibility structures, not evidence for the Japanese case.
